model: PeakNet (carbonscott/peaknet ConvNeXtV2-tiny-like [96..768]x[3,3,9,3] + BiFPN 256 + seg head), from scratch, 1 binary logit, log1p+std norm, saturated pixels zeroed

upstream.ref: d15a00a (feat: add feature vector extraction with GAP), editable install /sdf/home/c/cwang31/codes/peaknet

train.init: fine-tuned from pk_a step-3000 best.pt (pk_a: same model from scratch, 23 min on the same GPU, log /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/logs/h2/pk_a/train.log)

eval.eval_cmd: python -m seg.evaluate --model peaknet_baseline --config configs/peaknet_baseline.yaml --ckpt /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/checkpoints/h2/pk_b/best.pt --split test --workers 8 --save-overlays OUT --n-overlays 4 --out test_metrics.json  (config eval.val_thr -> val-picked threshold)

notes: Model code is upstream PeakNet unchanged (peaknet.modeling.convnextv2_bifpn_net.PeakNet, base.yaml architecture), only the head is 1 class. Trained with the shared seg/train.py: 512 crops (4 per image, 80% centred on a peak), rot90/flip + gain jitter, AdamW lr 3e-4 wd .05, cosine, focal(alpha .75, gamma 2) x10 + dice, bf16 AMP, best checkpoint by val peak F1 on 200 val images. History: pk_a (from scratch, saturated 65535 pixels only clamped) reached val peak F1 .571 at step 3000 with precision .40: the model fired on the unlabelled saturated pixel runs along panel edges. Fix (sat_zero 60000: saturated pixels -> 0 in the input adapter) and pk_b = 55 min fine-tune from pk_a step 3000: val F1 .756 @1k, .792 @3k, .820 @6k (best.pt), .796 @8k. Threshold: models are very confident, so val-best thr is 0.999; the eval picked it on every 2nd val image (732) over 0.9..0.9995, then ran all 1529 test images at that thr. Weaknesses: 1/4-res seg head (bilinear 4x upsample) blurs 1-2 px peaks (pixel IoU .22); recall is the limiter on test (R .785). Dead ends: patch_size 2 + learned ConvTranspose upsample (h1 pk_p2: val F1 .075, checkerboard speckle). Round 2 running: pk_c = fine-tune from pk_b, lr 1e-4, focal alpha .5.
